title: Jude and the Echo
premise: Gideon Kavanagh, a xenolinguist exiled to a forgotten listening post after her translations helped end the Fleet War, discovers the beacon she maintains is transmitting in a language that predates both fleets—and that she has been dreaming in it for years. When the ship Meridian returns from deep space with its crew aged backward into children who speak only that language, Gideon becomes the sole interpreter between two fleets poised to blame each other for what happened. To prevent war, she fabricates a translation claiming the phenomenon was natural, hiding evidence that the beacon's original builders—her own ancestors' generation—caused it deliberately as an inheritance test. As the truce deadline nears and the child-crew begins remembering forward again, Gideon must choose between exposing the truth that could shatter the fragile peace or burying it forever, and she ultimately reveals everything, gambling that the fleets' shared shock at their founders' deception will bind them together rather than tear them apart.
about_author: Lena Sterling is a former radio astronomer who spent six years at remote listening stations before turning to fiction full-time. Her work explores the languages we invent to survive isolation, and 'Jude and the Echo' is her third novel.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Asked For
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Establishes her solitary routine maintaining Relay Station Jude-9, translating routine traffic while secretly logging dreams in an unidentifiable language. She notes the beacon has been transmitting on its own for eleven days. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness beginning to crack.

chapters.title: A Ship Out of Time
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The Meridian answers her hails—crewed by children wearing adult uniforms, biologically aged backward twenty years. They speak only the dream-language. Gideon realizes she can understand them. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Both fleets demand custody of the Meridian; the truce gives her station jurisdiction as neutral ground. Commanders Voss and Adeyemi arrive with armed escorts. Gideon hides the children's language ability, claiming they're traumatized and nonverbal. Emotional beat: first deliberate lie.

chapters.title: Jude
chapters.summary: Child POV (the Meridian's youngest, whom Gideon names Jude). Jude experiences the station through the dream-language, perceiving Gideon as someone who 'speaks like home.' Establishes the children remember fragments of their adult lives. Emotional beat: trust offered without conditions.

chapters.title: What the Dreams Know
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Cross-referencing her dream-journals with the children's speech, she finds the language matches transmissions buried in the beacon's archive—predating both fleets by a century. Someone built this deliberately. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: Voss's Patience
chapters.summary: Commander Voss POV. Voss suspects Gideon is hiding something and pressures her with veiled threats about her war-record translations. Introduces the truce expiration: forty days. Emotional beat: menace wrapped in courtesy.

chapters.title: The False Translation
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Under pressure to produce findings, Gideon delivers a fabricated report: the age-reversal was a natural deep-space phenomenon, cause unknown, no fault assignable. The children corroborate her story, coached overnight. Emotional beat: relief shadowed by complicity.

chapters.title: Remembering Forward
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The children begin recovering adult memories in fragments—Jude recalls being the Meridian's engineer and seeing something in deep space: a structure, waiting. The memory arrives in the dream-language, which Jude now teaches Gideon properly. Emotional beat: childhood as a door closing.

chapters.title: The Structure
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Piecing together the children's recovered memories, Gideon learns the Meridian found an alien structure broadcasting the dream-language—a test or invitation left by whoever built the beacon. Her fabricated translation now actively conceals first contact. Emotional beat: the lie grows teeth.

chapters.title: Adeyemi's Doubt
chapters.summary: Commander Adeyemi POV. Adeyemi privately confronts Gideon: she doesn't believe the natural-phenomena report but suspects Voss wants the truth weaponized. She offers Gideon an alliance of silence. Emotional beat: unexpected kinship between liars.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Decoding the beacon's deepest archive layer, Gideon finds records showing the structure was seeded by the pre-war generation—both fleets' common ancestors—as a deliberate inheritance test meant to reunite their descendants. It failed; it caused the war instead. Emotional beat: grief for a hope that curdled.

chapters.title: Thirty Days
chapters.summary: Voss POV. With the truce expiring, Voss moves to seize the children, framing Gideon's station as compromised. A skirmish at the docking ring kills one of Jude's crewmates. Emotional beat: the lie's cost becomes blood.

chapters.title: What Jude Remembers
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude fully recovers her adult memories mid-childhood and must decide whether to keep speaking as a child to protect Gideon's fiction or tell the truth. She chooses to protect Gideon, at the cost of her own coherence. Emotional beat: found family demanding sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Interrogation
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Voss detains Gideon and plays intercepted recordings of the children speaking fluently. Her lie collapses. Voss offers her a deal: confirm the other fleet engineered the reversal, and Gideon walks free. Emotional beat: temptation of the easy exit.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon refuses and is confined, but Adeyemi smuggles her a message: the children have begun aging forward rapidly—the reversal is reversing itself, and when they're adults again, whatever they testify will end the truce one way or another. Emotional beat: countdown made flesh.

chapters.title: The Children's Fleet
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The children, led by restored-memory Jude, take over the station's systems using the dream-language the beacon responds to, locking out both fleets. They hold the station not as hostages but as witnesses. Emotional beat: powerlessness inverted.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Freed by the children's takeover, Gideon faces the choice: reveal the founders' deception and risk both fleets turning on the very idea of inherited authority, or maintain the lie until the truce simply lapses into cold war. Emotional beat: the weight of authorship.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, Gideon and Jude alternating POV. Gideon broadcasts the full truth—the structure, the founders' test, her own false translation—in the dream-language, translated live by the children so neither fleet controls the narrative. Fleets hold fire, stunned. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into testimony.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Truth
chapters.summary: Voss and Adeyemi POVs interleaved. Each commander processes the revelation; Voss rages, Adeyemi sees opportunity. The children, aging back toward adulthood, address both crews directly as living proof of a shared past. Emotional beat: anger searching for somewhere to go.

chapters.title: The Truce Renewed
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Instead of expiring, the truce is rewritten—not by treaty but by joint commission: both fleets will travel together to the structure. Gideon is asked to lead as xenolinguist, her exile formally ended. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Dreaming Forward
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, nearly adult again. Jude and Gideon prepare the Meridian for the joint voyage; Jude's memories have fully returned but she chooses to keep the name Gideon gave her. Emotional beat: identity as something chosen twice.

chapters.title: The Echo Answers
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, final chapter. As the joint fleet departs, the beacon shifts its transmission for the first time in a century—it is no longer repeating; it is responding. Gideon, surrounded by the family she never expected, sends back a greeting in the dream-language. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed as invitation.
